The outcome will be a structured, reusable test plan suitable for device certification, QA, and interoperability testing.

It fits the environment and requires minimal runtime/setup compared with heavier frameworks.

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Prepare global and workspace-scoped environment: verify python3/pip, ensure python3-venv available, write a workspace .env for non-interactive runs, optionally write /etc/profile.d snippet idempotently, and check for an already-running redis instance but avoid spawning orphaned daemons. Non-fatal broker checks allow broker to be started later by start/validation steps.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "python3 missing" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v pip3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pip3 missing" >&2; exit 3; }
# Ensure venv support present
if ! python3 -c "import venv" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo apt-get update -q >/dev/null && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-venv >/dev/null
fi
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE"
# Workspace-scoped env for non-interactive scripts
cat > "$WORKSPACE/.env" <<'ENV'
# Project env for CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub
CELERY_BROKER_URL=${CELERY_BROKER_URL:-redis://localhost:6379/0}
FLASK_ENV=${FLASK_ENV:-development}
ENV
# Idempotent /etc/profile.d snippet (do not overwrite if identical)
PROF=/etc/profile.d/coredoc_env.sh
TMP=/tmp/coredoc_env.sh.tmp
cat > "$TMP" <<'EOF'
# Optional global project env
export CELERY_BROKER_URL=${CELERY_BROKER_URL:-redis://localhost:6379/0}
export FLASK_ENV=${FLASK_ENV:-development}
EOF
if [ -f "$PROF" ]; then
  if ! sudo cmp -s "$TMP" "$PROF"; then sudo cp "$TMP" "$PROF"; fi
else
  sudo cp "$TMP" "$PROF"
fi
sudo chmod 644 "$PROF" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
rm -f "$TMP"
# Check for redis-server managed by system/service; do NOT spawn orphan daemons here
REDIS_RUNNING=1
if pgrep -x redis-server >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  REDIS_RUNNING=0
else
  if command -v service >/dev/null 2>&1 && service --status-all 2>/dev/null | grep -qi redis; then
    if service redis-server status >/dev/null 2>&1; then REDIS_RUNNING=0; else
      # attempt to start via service manager (safer than sudo nohup), non-fatal
      sudo service redis-server start >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      if pgrep -x redis-server >/dev/null 2>&1; then REDIS_RUNNING=0; fi
    fi
  fi
fi
# If redis-cli exists, do a ping; if not, skip here (will be validated later when venv deps available)
if command -v redis-cli >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if ! redis-cli ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "redis_unreachable_in_env_check" >&2
    # non-fatal here: broker may be started later by start/validation
  fi
fi
echo "env_ok"

steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
# Create idempotent venv
if [ ! -d ".venv" ]; then python3 -m venv .venv; fi
VENV_BIN="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin"
# Ensure pip available in venv
if [ -x "$VENV_BIN/python" ] && ! "$VENV_BIN/python" -m pip --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  "$VENV_BIN/python" -m ensurepip --upgrade >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
# Pinned requirements
cat > "$WORKSPACE/requirements.txt" <<'REQ'
Flask==2.2.5
pytest==7.4.0
celery==5.3.1
REQ
# Minimal Flask app (using flask CLI entry for better run behavior)
cat > "$WORKSPACE/app.py" <<'PY'
from flask import Flask, jsonify, request
app = Flask(__name__)
@app.route('/health')
def health():
    return jsonify(status='ok')
@app.route('/run-test', methods=['POST'])
def run_test():
    payload = request.get_json(silent=True) or {}
    return jsonify(received=payload), 202
if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=5000)
PY
# Celery tasks
cat > "$WORKSPACE/tasks.py" <<'PY'
from celery import Celery
import os
broker = os.environ.get('CELERY_BROKER_URL','redis://localhost:6379/0')
cel = Celery('coredoc', broker=broker)
@cel.task
def noop(x):
    return x
PY
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/logs" "$WORKSPACE/data" "$WORKSPACE/docs"
# Create empty SQLite DB file
sqlite3 "$WORKSPACE/data/artifacts.db" "VACUUM;" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# mkdocs scaffold
cat > "$WORKSPACE/mkdocs.yml" <<'MK'
site_name: CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub
nav:
  - Home: index.md
MK
cat > "$WORKSPACE/docs/index.md" <<'MD'
# CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub
Documentation placeholder.
MD
cat > "$WORKSPACE/.gitignore" <<'GI'
.venv/
__pycache__/
*.pyc
logs/
data/
flask.pid
celery.pid
GI
# Activate helper to source workspace .env and venv
cat > "$WORKSPACE/activate_env.sh" <<'ACT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE}"
if [ -f "${WORKSPACE}/.env" ]; then set -a; . "${WORKSPACE}/.env"; set +a; fi
# source venv if present
if [ -f "${WORKSPACE}/.venv/bin/activate" ]; then . "${WORKSPACE}/.venv/bin/activate"; fi
ACT
chmod +x "$WORKSPACE/activate_env.sh"
# Create start.sh that sources venv and sets PYTHONPATH/CWD before launching services
cat > "$WORKSPACE/start.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE}"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
[ -f "${WORKSPACE}/activate_env.sh" ] && . "${WORKSPACE}/activate_env.sh"
export PYTHONPATH="$WORKSPACE":${PYTHONPATH:-}
LOG_DIR="$WORKSPACE/logs"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
FLASK_LOG="$LOG_DIR/flask.log"
CELERY_LOG="$LOG_DIR/celery.log"
# Prevent duplicate start by checking pid files
if [ -f "$WORKSPACE/flask.pid" ]; then PID=$(cat "$WORKSPACE/flask.pid" 2>/dev/null||true); if [ -n "$PID" ] && ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "flask already running" && exit 0; else rm -f "$WORKSPACE/flask.pid" || true; fi; fi
if [ -f "$WORKSPACE/celery.pid" ]; then PID=$(cat "$WORKSPACE/celery.pid" 2>/dev/null||true); if [ -n "$PID" ] && ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "celery already running" && exit 0; else rm -f "$WORKSPACE/celery.pid" || true; fi; fi
# Start Flask via flask CLI (threaded) for concurrent dev usage without adding servers
export FLASK_APP=app.py
export FLASK_ENV=${FLASK_ENV:-development}
# run in background, log output
python -m flask run --host=0.0.0.0 --port=5000 --with-threads >>"$FLASK_LOG" 2>&1 &
echo $! > "$WORKSPACE/flask.pid"
# Start Celery worker with correct workdir and environment
CELERY_BIN="$(command -v celery || true)"
if [ -z "$CELERY_BIN" ]; then echo "celery_missing" >&2; exit 6; fi
# ensure worker runs with project PYTHONPATH and cwd
cd "$WORKSPACE"
CELERY_BROKER_URL=${CELERY_BROKER_URL:-redis://localhost:6379/0} "$CELERY_BIN" -A tasks worker --loglevel=INFO --workdir="$WORKSPACE" >>"$CELERY_LOG" 2>&1 &
echo $! > "$WORKSPACE/celery.pid"
exit 0
SH
chmod +x "$WORKSPACE/start.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
echo "scaffolded"

steps.name: dependencies
steps.description: Install pinned Python packages into the workspace .venv deterministically. Upgrade packaging tools inside venv, install requirements.txt with logs appended to logs/pip_install.log, record pip freeze to requirements.lock, and ensure pip log contains the installed version summary. Verify celery binary presence post-install (venv or global).
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
[ -f "${WORKSPACE}/activate_env.sh" ] && . "${WORKSPACE}/activate_env.sh"
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
[ -x "$VENV_PY" ] || { echo ".venv missing or invalid" >&2; exit 2; }
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/logs"
PIP_LOG="$WORKSPACE/logs/pip_install.log"
# Upgrade packaging tools and install requirements (append outputs to log)
"$VENV_PY" -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel >>"$PIP_LOG" 2>&1 || { echo "pip_upgrade_failed" >&2; tail -n 200 "$PIP_LOG" >&2; exit 3; }
"$VENV_PY" -m pip install -r requirements.txt >>"$PIP_LOG" 2>&1 || {
  "$VENV_PY" -m pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt >>"$PIP_LOG" 2>&1 || { echo "pip_install_failed" >&2; tail -n 200 "$PIP_LOG" >&2; exit 4; }
}
# Record exact installed versions
"$VENV_PY" -m pip freeze > "$WORKSPACE/requirements.lock"
# Append runtime summary to pip log for evidence
"$VENV_PY" -c "import sys; import pkgutil; print('python', sys.version.split()[0]); import importlib;\
try:\
 import flask; print('flask', flask.__version__)\
except Exception: print('flask not importable')\
try: import pytest; print('pytest', pytest.__version__)\
except Exception: print('pytest not importable')\
try: import celery; print('celery', celery.__version__)\
except Exception: print('celery not importable')\
" >>"$PIP_LOG" 2>&1 || true
# Verify celery binary availability (prefer venv)
VENV_CELERY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/celery"
if [ -x "$VENV_CELERY" ]; then echo "celery_in_venv" >>"$PIP_LOG"; else
  if command -v celery >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "celery_global_used" >>"$PIP_LOG"; else
    echo "celery_missing" >>"$PIP_LOG" 2>&1
    tail -n 200 "$PIP_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 5
  fi
fi
echo "deps_ok"

    exit 5
  fi
fi

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Validation: start services via start.sh (which sources venv), wait with timeboxed readiness checks, perform a fast celery inspect ping with timeout, run pytest as final verification, collect evidence logs, and perform supervised shutdown of started PIDs. Fail fast on critical issues while still dumping logs for debugging.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
[ -f "${WORKSPACE}/activate_env.sh" ] && . "${WORKSPACE}/activate_env.sh"
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
[ -x "$VENV_PY" ] || { echo ".venv missing" >&2; exit 2; }
# Start services via start.sh
"$WORKSPACE/start.sh" || { echo "start_failed" >&2; tail -n 200 "logs/pip_install.log" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 3; }
# Wait for Flask readiness (max 20s)
READY=1
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  if curl -sS --fail http://127.0.0.1:5000/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then READY=0; break; fi
  sleep 1
done
HEALTH_RESP=$(curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:5000/health || true)
echo "health_response:${HEALTH_RESP}"
if [ $READY -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "flask_not_ready" >&2
  tail -n 200 "logs/flask.log" 2>/dev/null || true
  # collect logs then fail fast
  tail -n 200 "logs/pip_install.log" 2>/dev/null || true
  exit 6
fi
# Quick celery inspect ping with timeout (do not block)
CELERY_BIN="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/celery"
if [ ! -x "$CELERY_BIN" ]; then CELERY_BIN="$(command -v celery || true)"; fi
if [ -n "$CELERY_BIN" ]; then
  timeout 5 "$CELERY_BIN" -A tasks inspect ping >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "celery_worker_responding" || echo "celery_no_response" >&2
else
  echo "celery_unavailable" >&2
fi
# Run pytest as final verification
PYTEST_LOG="$WORKSPACE/logs/pytest.log"
"$VENV_PY" -m pytest -q --maxfail=1 >>"$PYTEST_LOG" 2>&1 || { echo "pytest_failed" >&2; tail -n 200 "logs/flask.log" 2>/dev/null || true; tail -n 200 "logs/celery.log" 2>/dev/null || true; tail -n 200 "$WORKSPACE/logs/pip_install.log" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 5; }
# Supervised shutdown helper
shutdown_pidfile() {
  PIDFILE="$1"
  EXPECTED_CMD="$2"
  [ -f "$PIDFILE" ] || return 0
  PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [[ ! "$PID" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true; return 0; fi
  if ! ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true; return 0; fi
  CMD_NAME=$(ps -p "$PID" -o comm= 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$EXPECTED_CMD" ] && [[ "$CMD_NAME" != *"$EXPECTED_CMD"* ]]; then rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true; return 0; fi
  kill -TERM "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  for j in {1..10}; do if ! ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi; sleep 1; done
  if ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then kill -KILL "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
}
shutdown_pidfile "$WORKSPACE/flask.pid" "python"
shutdown_pidfile "$WORKSPACE/celery.pid" "celery"
# Collect evidence
echo "--- pip_install.log (tail) ---"
tail -n 200 "logs/pip_install.log" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "--- requirements.lock ---"
cat "${WORKSPACE}/requirements.lock" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "--- flask.log (tail) ---"
tail -n 200 "logs/flask.log" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "--- celery.log (tail) ---"
tail -n 200 "logs/celery.log" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "--- pytest.log (tail) ---"
tail -n 200 "logs/pytest.log" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "validation_ok"
